newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Index premiums firm ahead of data.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Index premiums firm ahead of data.

text.p: Premiums in major U.S. stock index options held firm Tuesday, thanks to a couple of important economic reports due Wednesday and Thursday, before August contracts expire, traders said.

"There's a lot of premium in here," said Jack Callahan, an independent market maker in S&P 100 .OEX options. "With the expiration, I look for some of this premium to come out but it's still a nervous market."
By 1215 CDT/1715 GMT, the spot OEX was up 2.79 points at 913.48, having bounced between 910.69 and 917.01.
The blue chip Dow industrial average .DJI was up 3.72 at about 8,066 and the S&P 500 .SPX added 1.84 to 938.84.
September S&P 500 futures gained 0.45 to 943, putting them about in the middle of their intraday range.
"There could be a big rebound, but there is concern about the downside," Callahan said, adding that a firm bond market helped to keep stocks' tone positive.
One OEX trader said investors were on hold ahead of the July U.S. producer price report due out on Wednesday and the July consumer price report on Thursday.
"Basically everyone is holding a steady course until they see how things look," the trader said.
"They don't want to take too much (premium) out of these things because it can blow in their face in a hurry if the numbers come out the wrong way," he said.

According to a Reuters poll, economists on average expect the producer price index to be up 0.1 percent after a 0.1 percent decline in June. They forecast the consumer price index to be up 0.2 percent after a 0.1 percent rise in June.
"Volatility's gone up this morning and the premiums have appreciated," Callahan said. "That's looking for the PPI tomorrow and the CPI Thursday."
Traders said despite the hesitation ahead of the economic numbers, investors did not hold back from rolling some options positions out of August into September.
"Today there seems to be a little more active on the rolls and the boxes than there was yesterday, although it's still fairly small," the OEX trader said. "Most people are pretty well rolled out."
In the August OEX series, trading was led by the 910 puts, which traded 5,755 contracts. The 920 call traded about 5,010 contracts and the 930 call traded 4,445. The August 900 put traded 4,430.
The most active September OEX contracts included the 900 put and call, the 880 put and the 870 put.
Among SPX options, the August 930 put traded 7,975 contracts and the August 950 call traded 7,625, making them the most active.
